Top rung matches solver2f proven 0.70 endpoint. Recipes re-solved and applied (--apply-solve, re-solve is a no-op); tech tree re-pegged. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED.
_predictions: PRE-REGISTERED. (1) REALIZED MARGINS SEPARATE BY RUNG. The n=3 baseline measured e0 23.5% / e1 24.4% / e2 22.7% - flat, which is WHY below-best is 55%. The design ladder acts on the recipe output:input ratio, which is the only margin lever that survives flat prices. Confident in direction; magnitude unknown because the AI arbitrages profitable rungs by building them. (2) BELOW-BEST FALLS from 55.0% (baseline sd 3.63pp). This is the metric the change targets. (3) PRICES: the user hypothesis is that higher margins normalise through PRICE DEPRESSION, i.e. the extra profit is competed away by overbuilding and F94 gap narrows. THIS IS THE INTERESTING TEST - F94 measured actual/design at 1.6-4.6x at the frontier. No confident direction: the same AI that overbuilds also stops when margins vanish. (4) GDP: no confident direction. Leaner recipes raise value added per level, but the baseline is nearly deterministic (0.9% spread over 3 runs) which suggests a binding constraint that a margin change may not touch. (5) NO PREDICTION on peasants or wall clock.
_comparison: PRIMARY: 20260829_212316_tier4-n3 (the same book, flat margins, n=3, spread 0.9% on GDP - an unusually tight baseline). SECONDARY: solver2f-n3 20260825_204213 (six rungs, rising 0.30->0.70). TERTIARY: vanilla n=16 20260821_131149.

(2) the four restored industries workers vs the n=1 run - the direct read on the fix. (3) below-best share and the per-era build allocation together. (4) PMR_JE| firings. (5) peasant share trajectory, especially the 1875-1880 divergence point where the first x1.4 cost step binds. (6) K trajectory and the 1935 endpoint.

_caveats: n=1 by ruling. The baseline is n=3 with a 0.9% GDP spread, so a GDP move outside ~1% is readable, but below-best has sd 3.63pp there and needs a bigger move to be believed.
